task: Multi-agent workflow that daily checks Google email and calendar, sorts the information, and presents an HTML daily briefing dashboard.

design.shape: Daily Trigger -> Inbox Analyst Agent -> Schedule Analyst Agent -> Chief Of Staff Agent -> Render Briefing Dashboard -> Email Daily Briefing
aiConnections: Inbox Analyst Agent.uses({ ai_languageModel: Briefing Model, ai_tool: [Gmail Inbox Tool] })
Schedule Analyst Agent.uses({ ai_languageModel: Briefing Model, ai_tool: [Google Calendar Day Tool] })
Chief Of Staff Agent.uses({ ai_languageModel: Briefing Model, ai_outputParser: Briefing Schema })
decisions: Agents chained sequentially rather than fanned out through a Merge node; the Chief Of Staff prompt reads the first report through a specific-node expression on 'Inbox Analyst Agent', which removes one node and the merge-mode configuration.
One shared lmChatOpenAi sub-node feeds all three agents instead of three separate model nodes.
HTML is rendered deterministically in the Code node from a schema-validated object; the agent supplies data, never markup.
Gmail tool query fixed to the last 24 hours of the primary inbox, and the calendar tool bounded to start-of-day..end-of-day, instead of letting the agents author their own filters.
autoFix on the structured output parser was dropped because it requires its own ai_languageModel connection.

Had to read the bundled ontology JSON in node_modules directly to obtain q, receivedAfter, systemMessage, maxIterations and the googleCalendar event:getAll shape.

The transformer parses .workflow.ts statically. Both a JSON.stringify(...) call for the JSON schema and a string-array join for the Code node's jsCode were rejected with 'Dynamic expression not supported in node parameters'.
